pr.title: Add assert_unsafe_precondition to unchecked_{add,sub,neg,mul,shl,shr} methods
pr.description:
(Old PR is haunted, opening a new one. See #117494 for previous discussion.)

This ensures that these preconditions are actually checked in debug mode, and hopefully should let people know if they messed up. I've also replaced the calls (I could find) in the code that use these intrinsics directly with those that use these methods, so that the asserts actually apply.

More discussions on people misusing these methods in the tracking issue: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/85122.
pr.author: clarfonthey

analysis.originalLogic: The unchecked integer methods forwarded directly to the corresponding intrinsics, e.g. `pub const unsafe fn unchecked_shl(self, rhs: u32) -> Self` contained `unsafe { intrinsics::unchecked_shl(self, rhs) }`, and internal code also called `intrinsics::unchecked_*` directly. The safety contract was therefore only documented, not validated by the `ub_checks` machinery. The PR changes each method to run `assert_unsafe_precondition!(check_language_ub, ...)` before the intrinsic, and replaces internal direct intrinsic calls with the methods so those checks apply.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Treating the unchecked arithmetic methods as pure intrinsic wrappers, or inlining/copy-propagating them as if their body contained only the unchecked intrinsic, drops the newly added precondition guard. The historical implementation did exactly this by forwarding directly to `intrinsics::unchecked_add/sub/mul/shl/shr`; for `unchecked_neg` it forwarded to `intrinsics::unchecked_sub(0, self)`. It did not emit the `UbChecks` branch and `precondition_check` call. A related incorrect transformation would be to retain direct intrinsic calls at internal call sites, since the PR states those direct calls must be replaced so the asserts actually apply.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust code invoking core's unchecked integer operations: `unchecked_add`, `unchecked_sub`, `unchecked_mul`, `unchecked_neg`, `unchecked_shl`, and `unchecked_shr`, including internal users such as `IndexRange`, `SliceIndex<[T]> for Range<usize>`, and pointer/`NonNull::sub`. Relevant inputs are values where the arithmetic result overflows, negation of `MIN`, or shift amounts `>= Self::BITS`; behavior depends on whether `UbChecks()` is enabled (debug/ub_checks) or disabled.
analysis.summary: This safety-fix PR adds `assert_unsafe_precondition!(check_language_ub, ...)` to all signed/unsigned `unchecked_{add,sub,mul,neg,shl,shr}` methods and switches internal direct intrinsic users to those methods. For the Inline pass, the important effect is that these method bodies now contain a `UbChecks` switch and a `precondition_check` call, which appear in Inline/pre-codegen MIR expectations when the unchecked method is inlined. This is not a change to the Inline algorithm itself; the regression tests were updated to retain the new guard in the inlined output. No compiler execution or reproduction was performed.
analysis.trigger: Inspect Inline output whenever an `unchecked_*` integer method is called and inlined: after this PR the inlined body must contain the `assert_unsafe_precondition` expansion, represented as `UbChecks()`, a `switchInt`, and a call to `core::num::<impl T>::unchecked_*::precondition_check`. Trigger the underlying safety bug only with program inputs that violate the unchecked operation's contract under enabled ub-checks (overflow, `MIN.unchecked_neg()`, or shift count not less than bit width).
preconditions: The build enables runtime ub-checks; the guard is controlled by `check_language_ub` and the `UbChecks()` query.
The numeric method body must use `overflowing_add/sub/mul(rhs).1 == false` for add/sub/mul, `overflowing_neg().1 == false` for neg, and `rhs < Self::BITS` for shifts.
Internal call sites must call the unchecked methods rather than the raw intrinsics, otherwise the method-level precondition check is bypassed.
`unchecked_neg`'s check is guarded by `#[cfg(not(bootstrap))]` because of ICE #125184 in the bootstrap compiler.
Pointer `sub` implementations use `(count as isize).unchecked_neg()` and therefore need `#[rustc_allow_const_fn_unstable(unchecked_neg)]`.
When `UbChecks()` is disabled, the precondition branch is inactive and the intrinsic remains the actual operation.
pitfalls: The shift precondition is strict: the patch uses `rhs < bits`, not `rhs <= bits`.
`unchecked_neg` is not implemented with a neg intrinsic; the old code used `intrinsics::unchecked_sub(0, self)`, while the new check uses `overflowing_neg()`.
Do not remove the `UbChecks`/`precondition_check` expansion when updating Inline test expectations; it is the safety check being added, not a spurious MIR artifact.
The Inline pass itself was not changed by this PR. The MIR test diffs change because the inlined callee body grew, so an expectation update must not be mistaken for an Inline optimization bug.
Direct intrinsic call sites elsewhere must be rewritten to method calls; otherwise the new checks do not cover them.
Do not test invalid unchecked operations in optimized/release builds as if behavior were defined; the checks are runtime ub-checks and the operation remains unsafe.
The PR's second patch only stabilizes `tests/run-make/libtest-padding/tests.rs` benchmark timing and is unrelated to numeric unchecked operations or Inline.
analysis.testStrategy: Use focused MIR tests rather than asserting execution: inspect `tests/mir-opt/inline/unchecked_shifts.unchecked_shl_unsigned_smaller.*` and `...unchecked_shr_signed_bigger.*` for nested `scope (inlined core::ub_checks::check_language_ub)` scopes, a `UbChecks()` call, `switchInt` on that bool, and `precondition_check(rhs, const Self::BITS)`. Also inspect `tests/mir-opt/pre-codegen/checked_ops.checked_shl.*` to confirm the checked path calls `unchecked_shl` with the extra inlined check scopes. For internal callers, compare `slice_index.slice_get_unchecked_mut_range` and `slice_index.slice_ptr_get_unchecked_range` MIR expectations. If constructing source-level tests, keep them under ub-checks/debug configuration and compare MIR generated with ub-checks on versus off; do not claim runtime reproduction without executing the compiler.
evidence: This ensures that these preconditions are actually checked in debug mode, and hopefully should let people know if they messed up.
I've also replaced the calls (I could find) in the code that use these intrinsics directly with those that use these methods, so that the asserts actually apply.
// ICE resolved by #125184 isn't in bootstrap compiler
_6 = core::num::<impl u16>::unchecked_shl::precondition_check(_4, const core::num::<impl u16>::BITS) -> [return: bb2, unwind unreachable];
